question: Where, when, and under which architectures, optimizers, and training regimes do recent neural-network parameter updates contain exploitable information about near-future motion?

key_findings.claim: Three probe families recover related but non-equivalent short-horizon structure in update trajectories.
key_findings.evidence: Across 30 CIFAR model-optimizer cells, element-wise sign agreement and future-subspace residual have median per-cell Spearman correlation -0.74, while DMD direction cosine and residual correlate at -0.75; 37% of tensor observations lie within 0.15 of the geometric DMD headroom bound.

key_findings.claim: Short-horizon predictability is strongly parameter-role dependent across both vision training and language-model pretraining.
key_findings.evidence: Vector-like auxiliary tensors exceed matrix-like bulk tensors in 29 of 32 matched trajectory comparisons under sign agreement and all 32 under DMD direction cosine; before temporal aggregation, the same ordering holds at all 246 Pythia model-checkpoint snapshots.

key_findings.claim: Bulk weights are not uniformly predictable, but contain sparse, localized, mostly transient predictable pockets.
key_findings.evidence: Under structure-aligned cuts and the stated isotropic reference, groups with residual excess above 0.3 make up about 6% of pooled group-anchor observations. Pocket identities usually turn over across anchors and their persistence differs by parameter role.

key_findings.claim: Parameter-resolved probes expose training events that a scalar loss curve does not localize.
key_findings.evidence: In Pythia-70M, bulk sign agreement falls below 0.5, head-aligned QKV residual excess largely fades around 20k steps, row-level low-residual pockets emerge later and first in deeper layers, and QKV sign agreement rises near the approximately 50k smoothed-loss minimum before peaking near 75k. The authors explicitly treat these as temporal correspondences, not causal evidence.

key_findings.claim: Architecture and optimizer recipe systematically reshape measured temporal redundancy, but higher predictability is not equivalent to better optimization.
key_findings.evidence: At matched loss on ViT-mid, SAM occupies the highest sign-agreement regime, Muon remains near 0.5, and Adam lies below SGD over most overlap. Across optimizer cells, rank correlation between mean bulk sign agreement and final accuracy is negative for every architecture (median -0.71); in the weight-decay ladder, the most predictable arm ends at about 0.707 accuracy versus about 0.755 for a lower-decay arm.

key_findings.claim: A narrow online check supports using the role-level separation as an eligibility prior for predictive write-back.
key_findings.evidence: Across three CIFAR-10 seeds, auxiliary-only eligibility improves mean accuracy by 0.94 and 0.87 percentage points on ViT-tiny and ViT-mid while accepting only 0.80% and 0.32% of parameters; full-scope eligibility accepts about 24% and yields smaller gains of 0.62 and 0.73 points.

method.core_idea: Treat predictability as a retrospective, parameter-resolved property of a stored training trajectory rather than as the score of one forecasting algorithm.
method.mechanism: At each anchor, use only the preceding five update vectors to measure sign persistence, cosine direction, containment of the next five-step displacement in a recent-update subspace, and explicit inertia, linear-trend, or dynamic-mode-decomposition forecasts. Compute probes at tensor and structure-aligned within-tensor scales, separate vector-like auxiliary parameters from matrix-like bulk weights, and calibrate group residuals against size-matched membership-permutation nulls.
assumptions: Stored checkpoints are close enough in time that five-step local history is meaningful; one step means one epoch for CIFAR and one 1,000-step checkpoint interval for Pythia.
Low-order direction and locally low-rank linear dynamics capture the relevant short-memory structure.
Grouping conventions correspond to meaningful spatial units; raw group levels cannot be compared across different cuts without calibration.
Pythia checkpoint trajectories and the controlled CIFAR panel are informative case studies, not evidence of universal behavior at larger scales or in other learning paradigms.
Retrospective association with loss or circuit events does not establish mechanism or causality.

techniques.role: Measures coordinate-wise sign agreement and magnitude-weighted cosine persistence from the latest update to a future displacement.
Measures how much future motion lies outside the span of a short update history.
Fits a standardized low-rank local linear operator to consecutive updates and rolls it forward to predict cumulative displacement.
Resamples group membership at matched geometry to separate temporal organization from chance residuals induced by group size and rank.
Cuts QKV heads and rows, attention outputs, MLP halves, convolution filters, and related units to locate predictable pockets.
Uses the auxiliary-versus-bulk measurement as a coarse online eligibility prior while retaining a coordinate-level safety mask.

evaluations.setting: 30 CIFAR-10 cells from five architectures crossed with six training recipes, 50 epochs, five reported anchors
evaluations.result: Median correlation is 0.83 for in-window versus future residual, 0.89 for DMD versus linear-trend selected sign agreement, -0.74 for sign agreement versus residual, and -0.75 for DMD cosine versus residual
evaluations.baseline: Alternative probe readouts applied to the same stored update trajectories

evaluations.setting: Pythia 70M, 160M, and 410M public trajectories, with broader appendical checks from 14M through 1.4B
evaluations.result: Auxiliary tensors win all 246 checkpoint snapshots under sign agreement and DMD cosine in the main panel
evaluations.baseline: Matrix-like bulk tensors in the same model and checkpoint

evaluations.setting: Structure-aligned bulk groups over CIFAR and Pythia
evaluations.metric: Future residual and null-calibrated low-residual group fraction
evaluations.result: About 6% of pooled group-anchor observations form the highlighted high-predictability tail, with mostly transient identities
evaluations.baseline: Approximate isotropic residual and membership-permutation null

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 online prediction under pure SGD, two ViT sizes and three seeds
evaluations.metric: Test-accuracy gain and fraction of parameters receiving forecast write-back
evaluations.result: Auxiliary-only eligibility gives +0.94 and +0.87 percentage points with 0.80% and 0.32% accepted; full scope gives +0.62 and +0.73 with about 24% accepted
evaluations.baseline: Ordinary training with no predictive write-back

limitations: Author-stated: probes capture short, low-order directional relations and locally low-dimensional linear structure, not arbitrary nonlinear, long-memory, or high-rank dynamics.
Author-stated: readings depend on checkpoint spacing, horizon, history length, grouping convention, and null calibration.
Author-stated: sign and residual probes use post-anchor displacement and are therefore delayed retrospective measurements, not immediately available online signals.
Author-stated: the controlled vision panel and public Pythia trajectories do not establish generality across larger models or other learning paradigms.
Reviewer-identified: many main comparisons are single-run trajectories; architecture, optimizer, and schedule effects are not fully factorial or seed-replicated.
Reviewer-identified: the online result covers only two CIFAR ViTs with pure SGD and does not isolate the role restriction from the much smaller accepted fraction or account for forecasting overhead.
failure_modes: Sign agreement can be inflated or distorted by exactly zero or numerically negligible coordinate motion, especially when cosine gives those coordinates almost no weight.
A flat arbitrary grouping can reverse an architecture ordering by mixing coordinates differently; raw low-residual fractions can contain large chance contributions.
DMD fails or is zeroed on degenerate histories and cannot represent future components outside the recent-update span.
Predictable-pocket identities can turn over abruptly, so a static mask may target stale coordinates.
Sub-0.5 sign agreement can indicate anti-persistence or cancellation rather than absence of temporal structure.
A high retrospective probe score can coincide with worse accuracy and should not be used as an optimizer ranking.
reusable_insights: Measure trajectory predictability at several geometric complexities before choosing a predictor; direction persistence, subspace containment, and forecast selectivity answer different questions.
Calibrate any group-level structure statistic against a null that preserves group-size and rank geometry.
Separate coarse parameter roles before searching for fine-grained pockets; vector-like parameters may be a safer first target for prediction, skipping, or compression.
Track the membership turnover of a selected subset, not only its population size.
Treat matched-loss comparisons as controlling elapsed progress only partially; optimizer state can still differ.
Do not equate exploitable redundancy with optimization quality.
open_questions: Do the auxiliary-bulk split and transient pockets persist in multi-billion-parameter pretraining at finer checkpoint cadence?
Can a history-only online detector identify pocket emergence and turnover without reading future displacement?
Which nonlinear or longer-memory predictors exploit structure missed by recent-subspace probes without becoming unstable?
Are sub-0.5 sign-agreement regimes caused by edge-of-stability oscillation, optimizer-induced mean reversion, or another mechanism?
Can adaptive write-back restricted by calibrated online confidence deliver wall-clock gains after predictor overhead?
How do predictable pockets align with representation formation, circuits, and interpretable parameter communities?

competitive_landscape.title: The Directionality of Optimization Trajectories in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Singh et al. characterize macro- and micro-scale directionality of raw weight paths and show late training can continue after freezing most parameters. This paper instead predicts short-horizon update displacement, resolves tensor and within-tensor locations, and adds subspace and explicit-predictor probes with geometry-matched nulls.

competitive_landscape.title: Predictive Differential Training Guided by Training Dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: PDT is an acceleration method that uses Koopman forecasts, parameter masks, and rollback scheduling. This paper is primarily a measurement study: it compares multiple probe families, asks where forecastable structure resides, and only appends a narrow online eligibility test.

competitive_landscape.title: Accelerating Training with Neuron Interaction and Nowcasting Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: NiNo trains a graph neural nowcaster that models neuron connectivity and reports training-time acceleration. This paper does not learn a cross-run graph predictor; it retrospectively diagnoses intrinsic local redundancy and finds it is sparse, role dependent, and time varying.

competitive_landscape.title: Introspection: Accelerating Neural Network Training By Learning Weight Evolution
competitive_landscape.difference: Introspection transfers learned weight-evolution patterns from simpler training runs to accelerate new models. This paper uses only each run's local checkpoint history and focuses on measurement, localization, calibration, and conditioning rather than far-future cross-run extrapolation.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the work provides the first convention-aware, multiscale framework that jointly measures directional persistence, recent-history subspace containment, and explicit local prediction across controlled vision training and one-pass language-model pretraining. Primary prior work already measures global trajectory directionality and uses learned or Koopman forecasts to accelerate training. Reviewer inference: the strongest novelty is the parameter-resolved measurement and null-calibrated localization of transient predictable pockets, plus the consistent auxiliary-versus-bulk split; neither DMD forecasting nor weight nowcasting is new. The online evidence is preliminary and does not yet establish a practical acceleration method.
reviewer_notes: All quantitative claims were checked against the main-paper page markers and the relevant appendices, especially pages 4-7, 41, and 42. Cross-regime absolute values are deliberately not compared because clocks and grouping protocols differ. Competitive records were verified on primary OpenReview or arXiv pages.
